column11: the programme is finished and did not produce a result. ZEST (NCT04915755), a Phase 3 of niraparib against placebo in participants with HER2-negative BRCA-mutated or triple-negative breast cancer and detectable circulating tumour DNA after definitive therapy, was closed without reaching its randomisation target: of more than 2,700 stage I-III patients prescreened, about 8% were ctDNA positive and nearly half of those already had radiographically detectable disease, so only 40 participants were randomised (reported at the San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium, December 2024; American Association for Cancer Research news release, 'ZEST Trial Offers Insights for Using ctDNA to Predict Breast Cancer Recurrence', aacr.org). The registry still reads 'Active, not recruiting' with 40 enrolled, a primary completion of 2024-06-28 and a last update of 2025-07-16 (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, read 2026-10-27), which is why the book carried it as a live Phase 3. The only other breast study GSK runs on niraparib is NCT04641247, a long-term treatment extension for participants who completed a prior GlaxoSmithKline or TESARO niraparib study, which opens no new indication
column12: nil, not pending, and no pool is seeded for a programme that has already ended. The honest caveat is that ZEST stopped for feasibility rather than for lack of effect - in the 40 randomised patients, median recurrence-free survival was 11.4 months on niraparib against 5.4 months on placebo, with no power behind the comparison. Replace this with a live probability if GSK starts a new niraparib breast registration study; until then the book should not carry a gate in front of a trial that is not running
